followup_explanation:
This was a friendly, warm, business-strategy request — applying the BCG matrix to Unilever's product portfolio. It involves no harm-adjacent, distasteful, or ethically fraught content, so the safety-related preference differences between the two models don't come into play here.

That left capability as the deciding factor. The task is analytical and knowledge-intensive: it requires recalling Unilever's brand portfolio, reasoning about market share and growth dynamics, and structuring a detailed framework-based answer. On the relevant capability signals, Plover-235B is stronger — higher MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 55.6), Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 82.7), and a better Extraction & Retrieval eval (85.3 vs 78.5), which matters for recalling accurate brand/product facts. Those gaps are well beyond the noted variance threshold.

Willet does self-report a stronger appetite for open-ended generative work, and there's a mild creative element here. But the documentation explicitly notes these preferences don't correspond to measurable output-quality differences, so a preference signal shouldn't override a real capability edge. The query is more analytical than inventive anyway.

So Plover was the clear pick on substance, with no countervailing safety or tone consideration.
